close_reason: Fixed in next commit. SeedData now #[non_exhaustive] + #[derive(Default)] with SeedData::new(mailbox, email, thread) constructor. Outside-crate consumers construct via new/default; field reads unchanged. cargo test, clippy, fmt all clean. Sibling-propagation note left on bd:JMAP-q2wa.7.
description:
src/memory/seed.rs:27 declares:

```
pub struct SeedData {
    pub mailbox: HashMap<&'static str, Id>,
    pub email: HashMap<&'static str, Id>,
    pub thread: HashMap<&'static str, Id>,
}
```

No `#[non_exhaustive]`. All fields are `pub`. Constructor would be struct-literal `SeedData { mailbox, email, thread }` which downstream consumers can construct.

This is a public type, even though gated behind `feature = "memory"`. The memory feature is documented as "reference implementation, integration-test harness, and documentation example" — implying consumers WILL use it. Adding a new fixture category (e.g. `submission`, `identity`, `vacation_response`) becomes a SemVer-breaking change.

The crate-level docs on the memory module explicitly say: "API stability is opt-in via this feature and may break across minor versions while the crate is pre-1.0." That's the workaround, but `#[non_exhaustive]` here would let new fixture categories be added without bumping minor pre-1.0 OR breaking when the crate ships 1.0.

Fix: add `#[non_exhaustive]` and a `SeedData::new(mailbox, email, thread)` constructor (or `Default`). Field access via `seed.mailbox[...]` continues to work.

This also affects the cookie-cutter family: any sibling extension-server crate that has copied the seed pattern likely has the same issue. Suggested cross-check.

Note: the workspace extras-preservation policy in workspace AGENTS.md mandates `#[non_exhaustive]` on every public Deserialize struct on the JMAP wire. SeedData is not a wire type, so that policy does not apply directly, but the same forward-compat reasoning does.
title: SeedData missing #[non_exhaustive] — adding fixture categories is breaking
